title: 10.5: Build a ParsePlan of ContractParser and RulesParser objects
description: Steps 1 and 2 of the cit parse algorithm: load the module files and rules sources, record where a rules name equals a module name (today just 'output'), and create a parser per input. Reporting moves into Orchestrate.parse so a library caller gets the same record as the CLI, rather than it living in __main__._parse. Plan: /Users/ntebaldi/.claude/plans/eventual-crafting-beacon.md (Step 3).
design: Both parser families become uniform -- constructed with their inputs, then parse() takes no arguments -- which is what makes step 3 a single loop over a flat list. ContractParser gains __init__(module, module_files). New frozen ParsePlan dataclass in cit.parse holds contracts: dict[str, ContractParser], rules: dict[str, RulesParser], and a 'both' property returning the sorted key intersection (the step-1 record step 4 will consume). ParseTarget is deleted: it modelled the old per-module rules pairing. DEFAULT_RULE_NAME is deleted with --rules. Reuse RulesParser.create, which already raises a ValueError naming the registered alternatives -- do not re-check the registry.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrate.parse(module_files, rule_files=None, *, strict=False) -> ParsePlan; one ContractParser per --module-file module, one RulesParser per --rule-file name; ParsePlan.both returns the sorted intersection; no parse() body is invoked; --rule-file nope=<wb> reports 'no rules parser is registered as nope (registered: output)'; a run with no --rule-file warns, and errors under --strict; Orchestrate.parse logs the contracts/rules/both summary under the cit.orchestrate logger and -v still reaches it; __main__._parse only rejects a missing --module-file, calls parse, translates ValueError to SystemExit, returns 0.

title: 10.0: Refactor Orchestrate to own every cit operation (mount per-call, run -> validate)
description:
Orchestrate was validate-only: it took the run mount as constructor state and exposed run() plus a per-module validate(). cit parse needs the same bundled-resource loading (contracts, rules, and the sources.yml registry from commit 4) but has no mount, so bolting parse() onto a mount-constructed object would leave a required constructor argument that one operation ignores.

This task makes Orchestrate the single layer between the CLI and the domain models: it caches the bundled resources and exposes one method per cit subcommand. Resource resolution stays out of __main__.py so that "which contract/rules artifact applies to this module" is answered in exactly one place, testable without argparse.

Not in the original plan for P1-10 (docs/planning/plans/contract-parser.md, commits 1-7) - it is a prerequisite refactor that lands before them, hence 10.0.
design:
- Drop __init__ entirely; no constructor state.
- run(...) becomes validate(data_mount, *, strict, modules, show_passed, show_files, max_files, checks) - keyword-only after the mount, which the CLI already passed by keyword.
- The old per-module validate(module, strict) becomes _validate_module(module, data_mount, strict), resolving the name collision. Private: no caller outside the class.
- Validator.discover() moves from __init__ into a _validators cached_property, so an operation that validates nothing (cit parse) never pays the discovery walk.
- iter_results(module) becomes iter_results(module, data_mount).
- Rejected: keeping the mount in __init__ and adding parse() (leaves a required arg one method ignores); a separate parse.py orchestrator (splits bundled-resource resolution across two modules, and duplicates it once sources.yml lands).
acceptance_criteria:
- uv run pytest and uv run ruff check both clean.
- Orchestrate() takes no arguments; the run mount is an argument to validate().
- One Orchestrate instance serves two different mounts without reloading contracts (regression test present).
- cit validate behavior unchanged end to end: test_synthetic_run.py passes untouched.
notes:
Implemented and verified on branch issue-11-contract-parser, uncommitted at filing time: 257 passed, ruff clean. Files: src/cit/orchestrate.py, src/cit/__main__.py, tests/test_orchestrate.py, tests/test_cli.py.

Deliberately NOT added, because their dependencies do not exist yet: the sources cached_property (needs find_sources_file + SourceRegistry, plan commit 4) and parse() (needs ContractParser.parse, plan commit 5). Both slot into the shape this task establishes - sources next to contracts/rules, parse next to validate. sources is the property that actually earns this refactor, so commit 4 should land before ContractParser.parse tests are written.

title: 9.8: Cache deduplication and simplify the accumulator loop
description:
GitHub: SWOT-Confluence/confluence-contracts#10
Plan: /Users/ntebaldi/Documents/workspace/confluence/docs/planning/plans/report.md
Epic: confluence-contracts-pj2 (P1-9). Follow-up on 9.2/9.3, landing on the same branch and PR #29.

WHY: Three small defects in Report's aggregation, found reviewing report.py after the epic landed.

1. deduplicated() runs TWICE per str(report) -- once in _counts_line (report.py:368) and once in
   _render_findings (report.py:397) -- recomputing an identical result. Measured on the real mount:
   12ms per pass over 6,664 findings, 36% of the 32ms render. Not a performance problem next to the
   223ms validation run, but a redundant second pass with no reason to exist.

2. __init__ stores the caller's list BY REFERENCE (self._findings = findings) while the findings
   property returns a defensive copy (list(self._findings)). That asymmetry is harmless while
   everything recomputes, but it becomes a stale-result bug the moment dedup is cached. Copying on
   the way in is the prerequisite for caching, and makes Report genuinely immutable.

3. The accumulator loop carries a redundant counter. Every iteration appends exactly one element to
   files AND adds exactly one to count, so count == len(files) is invariant for the whole loop --
   the counter holds no information the list does not. This is also what issue #10's first comment
   was pointing at when it suggested a defaultdict.

WHAT (src/cit/report.py only):
- __init__: self._findings = list(findings), so a caller mutating their list cannot invalidate the
  cache.
- Replace the five-line get/append/write-back accumulator with a defaultdict(list):
      entries: dict[Finding, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
      for finding in self._findings:
          entries[replace(finding, results_file='')].append(finding.results_file)
  DedupedFinding still gets both fields, both derived from the raw list: count=len(files) (raw
  occurrence count, duplicates included -- same meaning as today) and
  files=tuple(sorted(set(files))). No behaviour change.
- Move the computation to a private functools.cached_property named _deduped, and have the public
  deduplicated() return list(self._deduped) -- a defensive copy, consistent with the findings
  property, so a caller mutating the returned list cannot corrupt the cache for every later call.
  DedupedFinding is frozen, so only the list itself is at risk.
- Keep deduplicated() a METHOD. cached_property cannot decorate it directly: cached_property is a
  non-data descriptor that stores the computed value in the instance __dict__ under the same name,
  so the attribute resolves to the value rather than a bound method and deduplicated() would raise
  TypeError: 'list' object is not callable. Converting it to a property would be an API break at
  five call sites, three of which are in tests/test_report.py -- and the repository forbids editing
  tests to accommodate a change.

DO NOT cache grouped_by(): it takes a Callable key and lambdas hash by identity, so two call sites
passing equivalent lambdas would miss the cache every time while growing it unboundedly. Do NOT use
functools.lru_cache on any method here -- it keys on self and would keep every Report alive for the
process lifetime, which matters because _render_findings builds 5 throwaway Report objects per
str() (report.py:403) to reuse grouped_by across axes.

exit_code needs no caching -- it is a short-circuiting any().

OUT OF SCOPE: any rendering change, any CHANGELOG entry (the epic's existing [Unreleased] bullet
already covers this code; this is an internal refactor of code that has not shipped).
acceptance_criteria: deduplicated() returns the same value as before, byte-identical str(report) output on the real mount (1021 lines by default); deduplicated() computes once per Report instance and the second call returns the cached result; the list returned by deduplicated() can be mutated by a caller without affecting a later call; __init__ copies the findings list so mutating the caller's list after construction does not change the report; grouped_by is NOT cached; all 186 existing tests pass unedited; new tests cover the caching, both defensive copies, and the count==len(files) equivalence; uv run ruff check and uv run pytest pass.
close_reason: Follow-up design change (user-approved): deduplicated is now a public functools.cached_property returning tuple[DedupedFinding, ...] instead of a method backed by a private _deduped. Immutability (frozen DedupedFinding + tuple files) replaces the per-call defensive copy that a cached_property cannot provide. __init__ still copies self._findings. Updated 5 call sites (2 production, 3 pre-existing tests) plus Sphinx :attr: refs; replaced the now-moot defensive-copy test with one asserting immutability. Byte-identical real-mount output verified (1020 lines); 190/190 tests pass; ruff clean. Commit eb55baa (on top of 1e843ea, on d004e6b).

title: 9.6: Add a synthetic clean-run fixture and verify cit validate end to end
description:
GitHub: SWOT-Confluence/confluence-contracts#10
Plan: /Users/ntebaldi/Documents/workspace/confluence/docs/planning/plans/report.md
Epic: confluence-contracts-pj2 (P1-9). Sub-task 6 of 7. Depends on 9.5 (exercises the finished CLI).

WHY: The epic's first acceptance criterion is that cit validate runs end to end against a real mount,
and another is that a WARN-only run exits 0. NO CONTRACT ON THE MOUNT CURRENTLY PASSES CLEANLY:
momma.yml declares only stage and time_str while the files hold 39 variables, and output.yml was
seeded from a v16 granule against v17 files. So 'WARN-only -> exit 0' cannot be demonstrated on real
data and needs a small synthetic fixture whose contract matches its file -- worth building as part of
the test suite rather than hunting for a clean real file.

WHAT:
- A synthetic fixture (a small NetCDF written in a tmp_path plus a matching contract) whose declared
  interface agrees with the file, so the run produces WARN findings at most and exits 0. Follow the
  existing tests/conftest.py fixture conventions.
- A test asserting exit 0 on that fixture, and exit 1 once a FAIL is introduced.
- End-to-end verification against the real mount, recording the observed output in the commit or the
  bead's close reason:
    uv run cit validate --module momma --results /Users/ntebaldi/Documents/workspace/confluence/data/runs/end_to_end_mnt
  Expect a NON-ZERO exit for the reason above.
- Also verify --strict, --show-passed, --report PATH and --csv PATH behave on the real mount.

OUT OF SCOPE: fixing momma.yml or output.yml so they pass -- filling out the contract set is P1-14
(confluence-contracts-a08) and authoring momma.yml properly is P1-11 (confluence-contracts-iyu).
acceptance_criteria: a synthetic fixture whose contract matches its file yields exit 0 (WARN-only) and exit 1 once a FAIL is introduced; uv run cit validate --module momma --results <mount> runs end to end and exits non-zero; --report writes the same text that went to stdout; --csv writes a readable file; uv run pytest and uv run ruff check pass.
notes:
MEASURED CORRECTION -- the plan's stated expectation was WRONG, verified on the real mount after 9.5
landed. Do not chase it.

The plan (report.md:257-267) says 'Expect a non-zero exit' for momma and that no contract on the mount
passes cleanly. Actual, measured:

  cit validate --module momma  --results <mount>            -> exit 0   FAIL 0   WARN 39   PASS 3
  cit validate --module momma  --results <mount> --strict   -> exit 0   (identical; no-op)
  cit validate --module output --results <mount>            -> exit 1   FAIL 13  WARN 389  PASS 629
  cit validate --module output --results <mount> --strict   -> exit 1   FAIL 184 WARN 218  PASS 629
  cit validate                 --results <mount>            -> exit 1

WHY momma exits 0: undeclared file components are classified EXTRA/WARN, asymmetric BY DESIGN (see
validation.py's module docstring -- 'An undeclared component in the file -> WARN (drift)'). momma.yml
declaring only stage and time_str against a 39-variable file therefore yields WARN-only, which is
exit 0. That is correct behaviour, not a defect. Do NOT 'fix' it.

WHY --strict is a no-op for momma: momma emits 798 'contract' findings and ZERO 'rule' findings (rules
are the SoS artifact, which applies to output). --strict only escalates rule findings. On output,
--strict does work as designed: it moves exactly 171 findings WARN->FAIL (389->218 WARN, 13->184
FAIL), which independently confirms the plan's measured figure of 171.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS SUB-TASK:
- 'WARN-only -> exit 0' is ALREADY demonstrable on real data via --module momma. Assert it there.
- 'any FAIL -> exit 1' is ALREADY demonstrable via --module output, or the full run. Assert it there.
- '--strict makes rule warnings exit 1' is the ONE criterion real data CANNOT demonstrate, because the
  only module with rule findings (output) already exits 1 on structural FAILs alone, so there is no
  0->1 flip to observe. THIS is what the synthetic fixture is actually needed for: a case that is
  rule-WARN-only (exit 0) and flips to exit 1 under --strict.
- Also still worth the fixture: a genuinely clean all-PASS run (zero FAIL, zero WARN), which no real
  contract on the mount produces.
So the fixture's purpose is narrower and more specific than the plan implies -- build it for the
--strict flip and the all-clean case, not to prove WARN-only->exit 0.

Commit ac6b5c5 on issue-10-findings-report worktree branch (sits directly on 6774112). Added tests/test_synthetic_run.py: a synthetic NetCDF fixture + temp contract/rules YAML, discovered via monkeypatching cit.orchestrate.find_contract_files/find_rules_files (same technique as test_orchestrate.py) rather than adding a --contracts/--rules flag. main() runs unmodified -- real, hermetic end-to-end CLI runs. Achieved: (1) all-PASS clean run exits 0 (no real contract produces this), (2) introducing a dtype mismatch flips to exit 1, (3) a rule-WARN-only run (missing global attribute) exits 0 and the identical run under --strict exits 1 -- the one criterion real-mount data cannot demonstrate.   cit validate --module momma  --results <mount> --strict    -> exit 0  identical output (no-op, 0 rule findings)
  cit validate --module output --results <mount>             -> exit 1  FAIL 13  WARN 389 PASS 629
  cit validate --module output --results <mount> --strict     -> exit 1  FAIL 184 WARN 218 PASS 629
  --show-passed on momma: PASSED-only components 2 -> 4
  --report on momma: report file byte-identical to stdout (3123 bytes)
  --csv on momma: 798 finding rows + header, parses cleanly

Confirms momma exits 0 end-to-end (correct WARN-only behaviour per validation.py's EXTRA/WARN-by-design docstring), not the plan's stale 'non-zero' expectation. uv run ruff check: clean. uv run pytest: 186 passed (180 baseline + 6 new). title: 9.5: Build the real cit validate subcommand and apply the exit policy in main()
description:
GitHub: SWOT-Confluence/confluence-contracts#10
Plan: /Users/ntebaldi/Documents/workspace/confluence/docs/planning/plans/report.md
Epic: confluence-contracts-pj2 (P1-9). Sub-task 5 of 7. Depends on 9.4 (needs both output sinks).

WHY: cit validate raises SystemExit('not implemented yet') and its subparser has no arguments at all,
so the tool that exists to gate module PRs cannot be run or fail a build. main() also discards
args.func(args)'s return value entirely, so no exit code can propagate.

WHAT (src/cit/__main__.py):
- Target CLI:
    cit validate [--module M ...] [--results MOUNT] [--strict] [--show-passed]
                                  [--report PATH] [--csv PATH]
- --module repeats and defaults to every loaded contract, matching run(modules=...) taking an iterable.
- --results is THE RUN MOUNT, not a single file. That is what Orchestrate already takes and the only
  form that works for momma's 19 reach files.
- --report PATH tees the same human-readable text to a file; --csv PATH writes the 9.4 export.
- main() must exit with the report's code: print(report); sys.exit(report.exit_code).
- Report text goes to stdout via print and logging stays on stderr, giving a clean split: the report
  is pipeable, diagnostics are not mixed into it.
- Two logging fixes in scope, since this issue owns the story: logger = logging.getLogger('cit') in
  __main__.py is dead code today, and basicConfig configures the ROOT logger, so netCDF4 and pydantic
  messages at INFO would land in the user's terminal. Scope configuration to the 'cit' logger.
- -v/--verbose currently sits only on the parent parser, so 'cit validate -v' fails as an unknown
  argument. A parents= shared parser makes both orderings work.
- _validate currently raises the copy-pasted message 'cit parse: not implemented yet' -- it says
  'parse' inside the validate handler. Fix that (and leave _parse's own message for P1-10).

MUST NOT BREAK: tests/test_cli.py does build_parser().parse_args(['validate']) with NO other
arguments. So --module and --results cannot be required=True -- validate the combination inside the
handler and fail with a clear message instead. The repository forbids editing tests to accommodate a
change.

DROPPED, NOT DEFERRED: --contracts DIR and --rules FILE. They appear in the target CLI in
cit-details.md but work against the design -- contracts are the interface source of truth and ship as
bundled package data loaded through importlib.resources. A flag pointing CIT at a different set means
a green run no longer says 'this file matches the committed interface', only 'it matches whatever the
caller passed'. Changing an interface should be a reviewed commit to resources/contracts/, not a
command-line argument. Dropping them also keeps find_contract_files() and find_rules_files()
argument-free, so package data resolves in exactly one way. (9.7 corrects the doc.)

DEFERRED: --checks. Only two checks exist, Validator.discover() deliberately runs all of them, and
P1-16's report-only checks will need different semantics -- a selector now means building a filter
for a two-item list and reworking it immediately. The contract-linter mode (--checks rules with no
result file) goes with it: Orchestrate always streams from a mount, so a no-file mode needs a
different entry point than this issue provides.
acceptance_criteria: additions to tests/test_cli.py assert the new flags parse, that parse_args(['validate']) still works with no arguments, that 'cit validate -v' and 'cit -v validate' both parse, and that main() raises SystemExit(1) when the report holds a FAIL; no argument uses required=True; INFO logging from netCDF4/pydantic does not reach the terminal; report text is on stdout and log records on stderr; uv run pytest and uv run ruff check pass.
notes:
--show-passed SEMANTICS (defined in 9.3, which now groups component-first): the flag controls
whether fully-clean components -- those whose findings are all PASS -- appear at all. It does NOT
control whether PASSED lines appear, because by default a component with any non-PASS finding shows
its PASSED lines too, so 'what matched' and 'what differed' sit together. Wire the flag through; the
rendering decision lives in report.py.
close_reason: cit validate wired end-to-end: --module/--results/--strict/--show-passed/--report/--csv, main() propagates report.exit_code via sys.exit, logging scoped to the 'cit' logger, -v works before/after the subcommand. Commit e02bbd5 on worktree branch (built on 9481f64). 180 tests pass (171 baseline + 9 new), ruff clean.

title: 9.3: Render the report text: banner, legend, and component-grouped findings
description:
GitHub: SWOT-Confluence/confluence-contracts#10
Plan: /Users/ntebaldi/Documents/workspace/confluence/docs/planning/plans/report.md
Epic: confluence-contracts-pj2 (P1-9). Sub-task 3 of 7. Depends on 9.2 (needs dedup, grouped_by and
the _SEVERITY ordering).

GROUPING DECISION -- READ THIS FIRST. The plan document (report.md:33) specifies grouping by
SEVERITY, then module, then component. That is SUPERSEDED. Issue #10's first comment is authoritative
on scope and asks for the inverse:

  'Organize report by component type so it is easy to see all of the findings for one variable in one
   place - both what matched and what differed.'
  https://github.com/SWOT-Confluence/confluence-contracts/issues/10#issuecomment-5208729834

Severity-first cannot satisfy that, because one component's findings routinely span severities: a
variable can have a dtype DIFFERENT (FAIL), an undeclared attribute EXTRA (WARN), and four attribute
checks that PASSED (INFO). Severity-first scatters those across three sections, hundreds of lines
apart. Build COMPONENT-FIRST instead. Ignore the severity-sectioned layout in the plan's mockup
(report.md:151-168) -- note that mockup is itself internally inconsistent, placing a PASSED/INFO line
under a WARN heading, precisely because the point it illustrates is only legible when a component's
findings sit together.

WHY (the rest): The report has to be readable by a person gating a module PR. One line per raw finding
is 6,664 lines. Report also receives no version data today, but the banner needs Contract.version plus
source.branch and source.commit, and a run spans modules, so this is a version *set*, not a line.

WHAT:
- src/cit/report.py: implement __str__ (not a render() method -- the locked API is print(report)).
  All formatting is stdlib f-strings and str.ljust: rich and tabulate are not runtime dependencies.
- GROUPING: module -> produced-file template -> component -> that component's findings ordered by
  severity (FAIL, WARN, then PASS). Reuse 9.2's grouped_by(key) helper for each axis rather than
  writing a method per axis.
- COMPONENT ORDER: sort components by their WORST severity, so every component containing a FAIL
  appears before any WARN-only component. This is what preserves PR-gate scannability once the
  top-level FAIL section is gone -- a reviewer still hits the failures first, but each one arrives
  with its component's full context attached. Within equal worst-severity, sort by component name for
  determinism.
- PASS VISIBILITY (this is the point of the change): by default show every component that has at
  least ONE non-PASS finding, INCLUDING its PASSED lines -- that is what puts 'what matched and what
  differed' side by side. --show-passed additionally shows components where everything passed. So the
  flag now controls whether fully-clean components appear, NOT whether PASSED lines appear.
- EXPECTED SIZE, so nobody is surprised: measured deduplicated totals are 1,118 findings -- 486
  non-PASS and 632 PASS -- over 922 distinct components. The default view is therefore the 486
  non-PASS lines plus whichever PASS lines share a component with them, upper-bounded at 1,118 plus
  one heading line per shown component. That is roughly double the 486 lines the plan's severity-first
  layout would have produced, and is the accepted cost of the issue's grouping request. Still far
  below the 6,664-line raw output. Report the actual figure you observe when you run it.
- Keep the summary counts line (e.g. 'FAIL 58   WARN 428   PASS 632   1118 findings over 25 files,
  2 modules') -- with severity no longer being the top-level split, this line is now the only
  at-a-glance severity total, so it is load-bearing rather than decorative.
- Accept a version mapping alongside the findings: a dict[str, Contract] or a smaller
  {module: (version, branch, commit)} mapping. Orchestrate.run already holds self.contracts.
  Banner form: 'cit 0.1.0  .  momma  16.0 @ main 0123456  .  output  16.0 @ main 0000000'.
- src/cit/orchestrate.py: pass the contracts into Report, and delete the hardcoded __main__ block --
  it contains a personal absolute path.
- Print a LEGEND once above the findings. Every line is anchored on the same two nouns -- declared
  (what the contract or rules say should be there) and found (what the produced file actually holds)
  -- so the direction of a finding is never ambiguous:
    Declared = what the contract (structure) or the SoS rules (metadata) say should be there.
    Found    = what the produced file actually holds.
    PASSED     Declared and found, contract/rules match module file.
    MISSING    Declared, but not found in the file. Data is missing from the module file.
    EXTRA      Found in the file, but not declared. Extra data located in the module file.
    DIFFERENT  Declared and found, contract/rules do not match module file. Message indicates
               values for both.
  NOTE this wording deliberately corrects a direction error in an earlier proposal for MISSING
  ('actual module results are missing from spec'), which actually describes EXTRA.
  FindingType.MISSING means the FILE lacks something declared, not that the spec lacks something.
- Target layout under component-first grouping -- the momma 'nt' case is now adjacent BY DESIGN
  rather than by accident, which is exactly what the issue comment asked for:
    momma    flpe/momma/{reach_id}_momma.nc
      nt
        dimension  PASSED     x19 files
        variable   EXTRA      x19 files
    output   output/sos/{continent_id}_sword_v{number}_SOS_results.nc
      validation/offline/kge
        variable   DIFFERENT  x6 files
                   (contract dims: [...]) and (result dims: (...))
      reaches/time
        variable   MISSING    x5 files
  Since the component is now the heading, it comes out of the per-finding line, leaving the check,
  the type and the file count. Exact column widths are yours to choose.
- Grouping must tolerate a finding with NO file at all -- P1-17's cross-check is a registry lint
  that produces FAILs with nothing on disk behind them.

KNOWN OPEN QUESTION (decide during implementation): dedup keys on the finding minus results_file, so
an 'x5 files' line does not say WHICH five. For 'MISSING reaches/time x5 files' out of 6, naming the
odd one out is the actionable part. Preferred starting point: the CSV (9.4) carries every occurrence
and the text carries only the count; add inline listing only if it proves needed.
acceptance_criteria: print(report) produces the banner, the counts line, the legend, and findings grouped module -> file template -> component with each component's findings severity-ordered; components sort by worst severity so FAIL-bearing components precede WARN-only ones, then by name; a component with both a PASSED and a non-PASS finding shows both lines in one place by default (the 'nt' case); components whose findings are all PASS are hidden unless show-passed is requested; a finding with an empty filepath renders without raising (covers P1-17); output is byte-identical across runs on the same findings; orchestrate.py has no __main__ block and no absolute personal path; uv run pytest and uv run ruff check pass.

Added 12 new tests (test_report.py, test_orchestrate.py); measured against the real end-to-end mount: 1073 deduplicated findings (13 FAIL/428 WARN/632 PASS) over 25 files/2 modules render as 1021 lines by default. ruff clean, 165/165 pytest pass.   and correctly). Per cit-details.md these are unaffected by --strict as well as by the pass/fail gate.

title: Stop double-reporting fill attributes as attribute-level EXTRA

**P1-16 — Add the report-only health checks.**

Add two checks that report but never fail the run (exit stays 0, and `--strict` does not escalate them).

- **Completeness:** compare the produced file set against the expected reach/basin/set count from `reaches_of_interest.json`, and list any missing outputs — a module may have crashed on some reaches.
- **Non-fill:** for each required variable, report the fraction of non-`_FillValue` values, and flag a file that is entirely fill.
- Both land in the run report, not the pass/fail gate.

**AC:**

- A directory missing some reach files lists them in the report and still exits 0.
- An all-fill file is reported and still exits 0.
notes:
CARRIED OVER FROM PR #26 (P1-6 structural validator):

The structural validator deliberately does NOT compare dimension sizes - they vary per run,
and netCDF derives a variable's shape from its dimensions, so matching dimension names in
order is sufficient there.

The one case where a size carries information the names do not is a variable partially
written along an *unlimited* dimension: netCDF-4 reports dim.size as the max extent across
variables, so a short-written variable's shape is smaller than its dimension claims. That
is a silent partial-output defect and belongs in this issue's completeness check, not in
the structural gate.

Needs Netcdf.dimensions() widened to expose dim.isunlimited() (currently returns
{name: size} only) - consider a DimInfo dataclass mirroring result.VarInfo.

title: P1-3: Write the NetCDF reader
description:
GitHub: SWOT-Confluence/confluence-contracts#3
Plan: GitHub issue #5 (CIT Phase 1 tracking)
Epic P1-3 of P1-1..P1-17

**P1-3**

Write `netcdf.py` — the single layer that understands the NetCDF format. Everything that reads a
`.nc` goes through here; `result.py` never touches netCDF4 directly.

**Deliverables:**
- `open_nc` — open a NetCDF dataset.
- `iter_variables(ds) -> (qualified_name, numpy_dtype, dim_names, shape)` — walk every variable,
  descending into nested groups and qualifying names as `group/var`. **Structure only — no
  attributes.**
- `variable_attributes(var) -> dict` — all attributes on one variable, including `_FillValue`.
  _(added scope)_
- `global_attributes(ds) -> dict` — dataset-level (global) attributes. _(added scope)_
- the single `dtype token ↔ numpy dtype` map (`f4`/`f8`/`i4`/`i8`/`S1`), the bridge between a
  contract's `dtype` string and what NetCDF reports.

The attribute helpers live here (not in `result.py`) so netCDF4/format knowledge stays in one
module; `result.py` assembles its `variable_attributes` / `global_attributes` / `unit_fill_values`
from them. They are kept separate from `iter_variables` so a structural-only run pays nothing to
read metadata. Consumers: `RulesValidation` (`rules.py`) and `check_non_fill` (`validation.py`).

**dtype vocabulary sync:** `models.DataType` (the `Literal` `f4/f8/i4/i8/S1`) is the single source
of truth; the netcdf token map must not drift from it. Guard with an import-time check (`raise`,
not `assert` — asserts are stripped under `python -O`) that the map's keys equal
`get_args(DataType)`, plus a test that every token round-trips
(`numpy_to_token(TOKEN_TO_NUMPY[t]) == t`).

**AC:**
- On a sample `.nc`, `iter_variables` reports the right dtype/dims/shape for a scalar, an `[nt]`
  variable, and a variable inside a subgroup.
- `variable_attributes` / `global_attributes` return the file's attributes (including `_FillValue`).
- The token map and `DataType` are in sync (import-time guard + round-trip test).
